stops.title: Device, Inverter, Layout, Process
stops.body: Explore device structures, illustrative CMOS inverter circuits, schematic layouts and, in Process, how a device is made. The selected architecture carries across modes. Layout simplifies the layer stack and vertical geometry.

stops.title: Compare architectures
stops.body: Explore four device architectures on one possible scaling roadmap: FinFET, nanosheet FET, inner-wall forksheet and CFET. Tap an architecture button, or Compare to see the examples side by side.

stops.title: Orbit, pan, zoom, inspect
stops.body: Drag with one finger to orbit. Two fingers to pan. Pinch to zoom. Tap any layer to see what it's made of.

stops.title: Views
stops.body: Choose a preset 3D overview or a view along or across the channel. Presets vary by scene; architecture-specific details appear in the specialized views.

stops.title: Section
stops.body: Slide to cut the model open on any axis, or pull the layers apart. Display holds the sheet's see-through, slow rotate and the other display switches.

stops.title: Layers
stops.body: Hide any single layer to see what's underneath it — or hide a whole group, or everything, with one tap.

stops.title: Specs
stops.body: Read model dimensions and design notes. On individual Device scenes, tap a capacitance row to highlight the modeled coupling. Values are geometry-only estimates, not measurements or a field-solver extraction.

stops.title: Steps (Process mode)
stops.body: In Process, the Steps tab takes the place of Specs: every fabrication step with what it shows, the source it follows and what the model leaves out. Step with the arrows on the stage or press play. Show every operation adds the resist, exposure, etch and fill substeps; where the patterning routes part (the nanosheet's stack lines, the FinFET's fins), choose how they are printed: direct print, SADP or SAQP. The SADP and SAQP chips show those routes on their own, and Pitch walk lets the SAQP dimensions vary. The site selector switches between the nFET, the pFET and both sites, where the gate line ends in a gate cut or a shared gate. The Section tab's planes show a 2D section beside the 3D view, and a step that cites a figure compares it with what the source's text describes. The nanosheet and FinFET have flows so far; forksheet and CFET are coming.

stops.title: Story
stops.body: Read the concepts, trade-offs and limitations behind the architecture. Open About for Credits and linked Technical references.

stops.title: Step through the fabrication
stops.body: The stepper under the model moves one step at a time, or plays the whole flow. "STEP 6 of 18 · OPERATION 5" is the fifth operation leading into core step 6; switch on Show every operation in Steps to see them all.

stops.title: How a step stands against its source
stops.body: The badge beside the step number says how the state relates to its cited source: Source stage, Reconstruction, Teaching or Concept. Tap the step's name to open its full explanation, source and substitutions in Steps.

stops.title: nFET, pFET or both sites
stops.body: The pill at the top of the stage picks the device the flow follows. The pFET shares the nFET's early steps and then has its own masked steps; Both sites shows the two side by side, joined by their gate line.

stops.title: Section planes
stops.body: On steps with a source figure, Section lists named planes through the model. Pick one to see the cut in 3D, as a flat section, or both, with a small map showing where the plane sits.

learn.title: 1 · FinFET
learn.body: The gate wraps a vertical silicon fin on three sides. Start here: every later device keeps this idea and wraps more of the channel.

learn.title: 2 · Nanosheet
learn.body: The fin becomes a stack of horizontal sheets, and the gate wraps all four sides of each one.

learn.title: 3 · Forksheet
learn.body: A dielectric wall lets the nFET and pFET stacks sit closer together, shrinking the cell sideways.

learn.title: 4 · CFET
learn.body: The nFET and pFET are stacked on top of each other, so the cell shrinks again by growing upwards.

learn.title: 5 · Process
learn.body: See how a FinFET and a nanosheet transistor are made, step by step, from bare silicon to finished device.

glossary.name: Bottom dielectric isolation
glossary.text: A dielectric layer under the nanosheet stack that separates the channels and source/drain from the substrate, cutting leakage through the silicon below.

glossary.name: Contact etch-stop layer
glossary.text: A thin silicon nitride film laid over the source/drain and gate before the ILD. Contact etches stop on it instead of cutting into the device.

glossary.name: Chemical-mechanical polishing
glossary.text: Polishing that flattens the wafer, stopping on a harder layer; used after fills such as STI oxide, ILD and metal.

glossary.name: Contacted poly pitch
glossary.text: The gate-to-gate spacing with a contact between neighbours, the key horizontal pitch of a logic cell: about 45–48 nm at 3 nm-class and 2 nm nodes.

glossary.name: Equivalent oxide thickness
glossary.text: The SiO₂ thickness that would give the same gate capacitance as the real stack: the interfacial layer plus the high-κ thickness × 3.9/κ. Advanced nodes are below about 1 nm.

glossary.name: Epitaxial growth
glossary.text: Growing crystal silicon or SiGe on an exposed crystal surface, so it continues the lattice. The source and drain are grown this way: Si:P for nFETs, SiGe:B for pFETs.

glossary.name: Front end, middle and back end of line
glossary.text: FEOL builds the transistors, MOL the contacts that reach them, and BEOL the stack of metal wiring above.

glossary.name: Gate cut
glossary.text: Cutting a gate line so that two neighbouring devices get separate gates; the alternative is a shared gate joining them.

glossary.name: High-κ metal gate
glossary.text: A gate dielectric with a higher permittivity than SiO₂ (here HfO₂) under a metal gate, so the gate controls the channel through a physically thicker film with less leakage.

glossary.name: Interfacial layer
glossary.text: A thin SiO₂ film, under 1 nm in production, between the silicon channel and the high-κ dielectric.

glossary.name: Interlayer dielectric
glossary.text: The insulating fill, usually oxide, between devices and around the contacts.

glossary.name: Inner spacer
glossary.text: Dielectric formed in recesses of the SiGe layers at the ends of a nanosheet stack, so the gate between the sheets is kept apart from the source and drain.

glossary.name: Mandrel
glossary.text: A sacrificial printed line in SADP and SAQP. Spacers are formed on its sides, then it is removed and the spacers become the pattern.

glossary.name: Punch-through stopper
glossary.text: A heavily doped region under the fin or stack that blocks leakage from source to drain through the substrate below the gate.

glossary.name: Pitch walk
glossary.text: Unequal spaces between lines from multiple patterning, caused when the core or spacer widths drift from their ideal values.

glossary.name: Channel release
glossary.text: Selectively etching away the SiGe layers of a nanosheet stack to free the silicon sheets, so the gate can wrap all four sides.

glossary.name: Replacement metal gate
glossary.text: A gate-last flow: a sacrificial dummy gate holds the place during the hot steps, then is removed and replaced by the high-κ/metal gate.

glossary.name: Self-aligned double / quadruple patterning
glossary.text: Spacers formed on printed mandrels become the pattern, halving the printed pitch (SADP) or, repeated once more, quartering it (SAQP).

glossary.name: Silicide
glossary.text: A metal–silicon compound at the bottom of a contact (here TiSiₓ) that lowers the contact resistance.

glossary.name: Shallow trench isolation
glossary.text: Oxide-filled trenches that separate neighbouring active areas.

glossary.name: Work-function metal
glossary.text: A thin metal in the gate that sets the transistor's threshold voltage: an n-type one for nFETs, typically TiN for pFETs.

glossary.name: Effective width
glossary.text: The total gated channel perimeter that carries current: for a fin, twice the height plus the top width; for sheets, the sum of the sheet perimeters.
